# ExplodeEmptySeparator

<Badge type="danger" text="error" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Detect explode with a separator statically equal to the empty string.

## Example

```php{2}
<?php
$parts=explode('',$text);
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Supply a nonempty separator.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Report explode with a separator statically equal to the empty string.
- Resolve builtin calls and named arguments before checking the contract. Project-local callees are considered only when their bodies or immutable summaries establish the required facts. The default is enabled, with positive proof required.
- For flow-dependent conditions, require a reachable source-to-use path with no intervening invalidation. Unknown calls, ambiguous aliases or recursion cannot establish definite facts. When the proof is inconclusive, nothing is reported.
- A separator read from a variable is definite only when plain assignments are the sole way that variable can change in the scope of the call. See E3 for the writes that make it indefinite.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Unknown or nonempty separators and shadowed application functions are excluded.
- Unresolved targets, incomplete required facts, suppressed findings and PHP versions lacking the referenced API or language feature produce no report. User declarations shadowing builtin names are not builtin contracts.
- E3. No report when a variable of the separator expression cannot be trusted. Each such variable is proven only while nothing in its scope can change it behind its plain assignments, anywhere and in any statement order: `++` or `--` on it or on one of its elements; a `catch`, `foreach` key or value binding it; a reference to it (a by-reference assignment on either side, a by-reference `foreach` over it, a by-reference array item, a by-reference capture by a nested closure, or an argument, other than the inspected argument itself, that a resolved callee binds by reference or that a callee custos cannot resolve receives); a write naming its target at run time (a variable variable, `extract()`, one-argument `parse_str()` or `mb_parse_str()`, `include`/`require`, `eval`); or a `$GLOBALS` access other than a literal entry naming another variable. A `global` or `static` declaration of it, or a by-reference capture by the closure that is the scope, removes the proof too. In top-level code, where locals are globals, a `global` declaration naming it in any function of the file, or a `$GLOBALS` access anywhere in the file, does as well. The same holds for every local whose value an assignment stores into it, whatever the assigned expression computes, directly or through further assignments. A read inside an arrow function also checks the scopes the arrow function captures from. Incrementing an empty string yields `"1"`.

  The check is lexical and deliberately conservative: it does not prove that the rewriting code runs between the assignment and the call.

## Fix

No automatic fix: byte splitting, code-point splitting and grapheme splitting are different contracts.

## PHP versions

Apply only on PHP versions supporting the referenced APIs and syntax (within PHP 5.3–8.5). Builtin behavior and argument contracts follow the configured PHP version. Extension-specific calls require resolved extension API symbols; do not treat same-named application functions as extension calls.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "ExplodeEmptySeparator": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore ExplodeEmptySeparator
```
